panels.shot: epic split-panel style wide, half showing a Mughal camp before Purandar, half a dim tent council
panels.action: On one side Mirza Raja Jai Singh I stands before the looming bulk of Purandar Fort, ranks of Mughal tents and siege lines behind him; on the other side Shivaji sits in a lamplit war council within the fort, maps spread before him, both men locked in a tense, unseen confrontation across space.

dialogue.text: In the summer of 1665, while Aurangzeb pressed the Deccan, Mirza Raja Jai Singh and Shivaji turned the storm around Purandar into a bargain that reshaped Maratha and Mughal power.

i18n.hi: १६६५ की गर्मियों में, जब औरंगज़ेब दक्कन दबा रहा था, मिर्ज़ा राजा जयसिंह और शिवाजी ने पुरंदर के तूफ़ान को ऐसे सौदे में बदला जिसने मराठा–मुग़ल ताक़त का नक्शा बदल दिया।

panels.shot: high aerial wide over the Deccan plateau
panels.action: A sweeping bird’s‑eye view shows the rugged hills near Pune, dotted with Maratha hill forts; in the distance a vast Mughal army under Jai Singh I advances like a dark river across the dusty plains toward the Purandar massif.

dialogue.text: Aurangzeb had just taken the Mughal throne. To tame the Deccan, he turned to Mirza Raja Jai Singh, the seasoned Rajput general, and pointed him toward Shivaji’s hill forts near Pune.

i18n.hi: तख़्त पर अभी-अभी औरंगज़ेब बैठा था। दक्कन को काबू करने के लिए उसने बूढ़े रणबाज़ राजपूत, मिर्ज़ा राजा जयसिंह को बुलाया और उसे पुणे के पास शिवाजी के गढ़ों पर टूट पड़ने को कहा।

panels.shot: medium close on Jai Singh in his command tent
panels.action: Inside a richly furnished yet austere Mughal command tent, Jai Singh I studies a detailed map of the Pune region, marked with small model forts, while officers stand in respectful silence; his face is calm, calculating, neither harsh nor lax.

dialogue.text: In his letters to Aurangzeb, Jai Singh warned that Shivaji’s forts were the spine of Maratha power. The Rajput chose not a single glorious charge, but a careful net around those rocky citadels.

i18n.hi: औरंगज़ेब को लिखे ख़तों में जयसिंह ने चेताया—शिवाजी के किले ही मराठा ताक़त की रीढ़ हैं। राजपूत ने एक ही धावा नहीं, बल्कि उन पथरीले दुर्गों पर जाल कसने की चाल चुनी।

panels.shot: ground-level wide of multiple fort lines
panels.action: From the vantage of a hillside, we see several Maratha forts—Purandar, Vajragad and other outworks—each on its own crag, while long lines of Mughal troops and artillery snake into valleys between them, building trenches and batteries.

dialogue.text: By March 1665, Mughal detachments moved like fingers into the Sahyadri hills. Jai Singh’s plan, recorded in his dispatches, was to isolate Purandar by taking its satellite posts one by one.

i18n.hi: मार्च १६६५ तक, मुग़ल टुकड़ियाँ सह्याद्री में उंगलियों-सी घुस चलीं। जयसिंह की योजना, उसके हुज़ूरनामों में दर्ज, पुरंदर को उसकी हर चौकी एक-एक कर काटकर बिल्कुल अकेला करना था।

panels.shot: interior medium of Shivaji in Purandar council
panels.action: Inside a stone hall of Purandar Fort, Shivaji sits cross‑legged with his commanders; Murarbaji Deshpande, stern and broad‑shouldered, points toward the window slit where smoke from Mughal camps rises in the distance.

dialogue.text: Within Purandar, Shivaji weighed each move. Sabhasad’s Bakhar remembers his words to Murarbaji Deshpande: hold the fort, bleed the enemy, and buy time while he gauged Jai Singh’s true intent.

i18n.hi: पुरंदर के भीतर शिवाजी हर चाल तोल रहे थे। सभासद की बखर में उसके मुरारबाजी देशपांडे से शब्द दर्ज हैं: गढ़ पकड़े रख, दुश्मन को खून से भर दे, और तब तक वक़्त खरीद जब तक मैं जयसिंह की असली नीयत परखूँ।

panels.shot: low-angle wide from Mughal trenches looking up at Purandar
panels.action: From a muddy Mughal trench, soldiers strain at ropes to drag a heavy cannon into position; above them Purandar looms, its stone ramparts lined with tiny figures of Maratha defenders, the sky hazy with dust.

dialogue.text: The Mughal records speak of trenches dug, batteries raised, and supplies hauled up under fire. This was not a raider’s skirmish, but slow, grinding siege craft brought to the Deccan hills.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल दफ़्तरों में खाइयाँ, तोपचौकियाँ और गोलाबारूद ढोने के क़िस्से दर्ज हैं। यह कोई लुटेरे की झड़प नहीं, बल्कि दक्कन की पहाड़ियों पर रेंगती किलेबंदी की घेराबंदी थी।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-action wide on Murarbaji leading a sortie
panels.action: With the fort gate open behind him, Murarbaji Deshpande charges out with a band of Maratha soldiers, shields raised and faces set, rushing downhill toward advancing Mughal infantry who brace for the impact.

dialogue.text: Sabhasad paints Murarbaji as the storm of Purandar, leading furious sorties down the slopes. For weeks his small bands harried Mughal trenches, making every yard of ground costlier.

i18n.hi: सभासद मुरारबाजी को पुरंदर का तूफ़ान बनाकर दिखाता है, जो ढलानों से गरजते धावे करवाता है। हफ्तों उसकी टुकड़ियाँ मुग़ल खाइयों पर टूटती रहीं, हर हाथ ज़मीन महँगा कर दिया।

panels.shot: close three-quarter on Jai Singh observing battlefield from a rise
panels.action: Jai Singh stands on a low ridge, flanked by officers, watching dust clouds rise where Murarbaji’s men clash with his troops; his expression is intent, admiring yet uncompromising, as he gives measured orders.

dialogue.text: Jai Singh’s letters do not dwell on Murarbaji, but they note stout resistance. The Rajput commander pressed on, bringing fresh contingents, adjusting routes, closing every path that might relieve Purandar.

i18n.hi: जयसिंह के खतों में मुरारबाजी पर ज़्यादा रंग नहीं, पर ज़बरदस्त रोक का ज़िक्र है। राजपूत सरदार आगे बढ़ता गया, नए दल खींचता, राहें बदलता, पुरंदर को राहत की हर राह बंद करता गया।

panels.shot: intense mid-shot skirmish on the slopes below Purandar
panels.action: On a narrow rocky ledge under the fort walls, Murarbaji and his men clash in close quarters with Mughal troops; the image freezes at a moment of strain and exhaustion, faces lined, dust hanging heavy.

dialogue.text: Accounts differ on each assault, but they agree on this: in a fierce fight on Purandar’s lower works, Murarbaji fell. His death broke the fort’s fiercest edge, even as his name entered Maratha memory.

i18n.hi: हर धावे की कहानी अलग, पर इस पर सब सहमत हैं—पुरंदर के निचले बाँकों पर भयंकर भिड़ंत में मुरारबाजी ढेर हुआ। उसकी मौत ने गढ़ की सबसे धारदार तलवार कुंद की, पर नाम मराठा याद में बस गया।

panels.shot: somber interior medium on Shivaji receiving news
panels.action: In a dim chamber, a tired messenger bows before Shivaji, who sits very still, one hand tightening on his sword hilt; outside the narrow window, smoke from Mughal guns curls up past the stone.

dialogue.text: Jedhe Shakavali notes the loss of Purandar’s commander. Shivaji, hearing of Murarbaji’s end and the tightening ring, now faced a choice between heroic ruin and a bargain on harsh terms.

i18n.hi: जेडे शकावली में पुरंदर के सरदार के खोने का लेखा है। मुरारबाजी की मौत और घेरती फाँस की ख़बर सुनकर शिवाजी के सामने अब दो राहें थीं—शौर्यभरी तबाही या कड़ी शर्तों पर सौदा।

panels.shot: medium inside Jai Singh's tent as an envoy bows
panels.action: Inside Jai Singh’s command tent, a Maratha envoy bows deeply, while Jai Singh sits upright on a low seat, hands resting on his knees, his face composed as he listens.

dialogue.text: Around this time, talks began. Mughal dispatches present Jai Singh as the calm victor offering terms; Maratha bakhars remember Shivaji as the strategist, bargaining to save his core strength.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं दिनों बात-चीत शुरू हुई। मुग़ल हुज़ूरनामे जयसिंह को ठंडे दिमाग का विजेता दिखाते हैं; मराठा बखरें शिवाजी को रणनीतिकार मानती हैं, जो अपने असली बल को बचाने के लिए सौदा कर रहा था।

panels.shot: tight interior wide of the first face-to-face meeting
panels.action: In a spacious tent hung with simple carpets, Jai Singh and Shivaji sit facing each other on low cushions, attendants drawn back to the edges; between them lies a spread of maps and lists of forts.

dialogue.text: Raja Jai Singh: "Let us make such peace that neither throne need fear the other’s shadow."

i18n.hi: राजा जयसिंह: "ऐसा सुलह करें कि दोनों तख़्त एक-दूसरे की परछाईं से भी न डरें।"

panels.shot: medium close on Shivaji listening, half-profile of Jai Singh
panels.action: Shivaji listens intently, eyes narrowed, while Jai Singh gestures lightly toward the maps; the lamp between them throws their faces into sharp relief, unity and mistrust sharing the same space.

dialogue.text: European observer Manucci later wrote of Jai Singh’s skill with words. Yet each side’s chroniclers lay the credit at their own hero’s feet, a reminder that treaties are stories as much as signatures.

i18n.hi: यूरोपी पर्यवेक्षक मनुच्ची ने बाद में जयसिंह की ज़बान की फनकारी लिखी। मगर दोनों तरफ़ के लिहाज़ अपने-अपने नायक को ही श्रेय देते हैं, याद दिलाते हुए कि संधियाँ दस्तख़त जितनी, कहानी भी होती हैं।

panels.shot: diagrammatic overhead-style wide of forts being marked on a map
panels.action: A close view of a parchment map shows small fort symbols; Jai Singh’s hand moves black stones onto one side, while Shivaji’s hand guards a cluster of remaining forts, highlighting a division of territories.

dialogue.text: The Purandar treaty of June 1665 is clear: Shivaji ceded 23 forts to the empire, retained 12, agreed to serve in person, and saw his son Sambhaji enter the Mughal ranks as a mansabdar.

i18n.hi: जून १६६५ की पुरंदर संधि साफ थी: शिवाजी ने २३ किले बादशाह को सौंपे, १२ रखे, खुद हाज़िरख़िदमत होने पर राज़ी हुआ और उसका बेटा संभाजी मुग़ल फौज में मनसबदार बना।

panels.shot: exterior wide of Mughal flag over surrendered outwork, distant forts still Maratha
panels.action: On a captured outwork near Purandar, Mughal soldiers raise an imperial standard over the stone bastion, while far in the background, atop another peak, a Maratha flag still flutters stubbornly.

dialogue.text: Imperial farmans praised Jai Singh’s success: Purandar’s fall, forts yielded, a troublesome power brought to heel. For Aurangzeb, it was a step toward a firmer Deccan frontier under imperial colors.

i18n.hi: शाही फ़रमानों ने जयसिंह की फ़तह का गुणगान किया—पुरंदर का पतन, किले सुपुर्द, सिर उठाती ताक़त झुका दी गई। औरंगज़ेब के लिए यह दक्कन में सख़्त सरहद की ओर एक क़दम था।

panels.shot: quiet interior medium on Shivaji with his close followers
panels.action: Back within a fort hall, Shivaji speaks softly to a small circle of trusted men; some look troubled, others relieved, as he rests his hand on a rolled copy of the treaty.

dialogue.text: Shivaji: "We yield stone to save strength. The hills will wait for our return."

i18n.hi: शिवाजी: "पत्थर छोड़ते हैं, ताक़त बचाते हैं। ये पहाड़ हमारी वापसी का इंतज़ार करेंगे।"

panels.shot: medium on Jai Singh writing a dispatch by lamplight
panels.action: At night in his tent, Jai Singh writes by lamplight, a scribe beside him; behind, a rolled banner and a sword rest against the pole, hinting at both victory and further duty.

dialogue.text: In his report, Jai Singh urged Aurangzeb to keep this new balance, to use Shivaji’s loyalty rather than drive him back to rebellion. His concern was not only conquest, but a workable settlement.

i18n.hi: अपनी रिपोर्ट में जयसिंह ने औरंगज़ेब से कहा कि इस नए संतुलन को थामे रखो, शिवाजी की वफ़ादारी से काम लो, उसे फिर बगावत की तरफ़ मत धकेलो। उसकी नज़र सिर्फ़ फ़तह पर नहीं, चलने लायक समझौते पर भी थी।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide, Purandar in changing light
panels.action: Purandar Fort stands silent in the shifting light of dawn to dusk, its walls unchanged while tiny figures—first Mughal, then Maratha—come and go along its ramparts over time.

dialogue.text: Later events would shatter this fragile peace. Yet in 1665, Purandar had shown that a fort could fall not only to cannon, but to negotiation, each side believing it had outplayed the other.

i18n.hi: आगे की आँधियों ने इस नाज़ुक सुलह को तोड़ डाला। पर १६६५ का पुरंदर दिखा चुका था कि किले सिर्फ़ तोप से नहीं, सौदे से भी गिरते हैं—जब दोनों तरफ़ को लगता रहे कि असली बाज़ी उसने जीती।

panels.shot: paired close-ups, split frame of Jai Singh and Shivaji looking in opposite directions
panels.action: A split close-up shows Jai Singh gazing northward with a thoughtful, slightly burdened expression, and Shivaji looking toward the western hills, eyes alight with quiet resolve, their profiles never quite meeting.

dialogue.text: Purandar under Jai Singh stands as a moment when siege turned into diplomacy, and when both a Rajput general and a Maratha king used the same treaty as a step toward very different futures.

i18n.hi: जयसिंह के अधीन पुरंदर वो पल है जब घेरा कूटनीति में बदला, और जब एक राजपूत सरदार और एक मराठा राजा ने एक ही संधि को दो बिल्कुल अलग भविष्य की सीढ़ी बनाया।

subtitle_i18n.hi: जब किले बने सौदे की मेज़
